knowledge:
- key_parameters: Y=numeric or factor vector of phenotype values (0/1 for case-control) ;; snps1=SnpMatrix object or data.frame containing the SNPs of the first gene ;; snps2=SnpMatrix object or data.frame containing the SNPs of the second gene ;; method=character string specifying the GGI method to use (e.g., "PCA", "CCA", "PLSPM", "U", "minP", "maxT") ;; nperm=number of permutations for permutation-based methods
- alternatives: PLINK=preferred for fast, genome-wide single SNP-SNP interaction screening ;; GBIGM=preferred for entropy-based gene-gene interaction analysis
- when_to_use: When analyzing case-control genomic data to detect statistical interactions between pairs of genes, aggregating multiple SNP-SNP interactions into a single gene-level test statistic.
- pitfalls: Using high-dimensional methods like CCA or PLSPM on genes with very few SNPs or high collinearity without checking model assumptions ;; High computational overhead when running permutation tests (nperm) on large cohorts ;; Missing data in SnpMatrix objects which must be imputed beforehand.

workflows.name: gene_gene_interaction_testing
workflows.intent: Test for statistical interaction between two genes represented by sets of SNPs in a case-control study.
input: gene1_snps.csv (genotype matrix for SNPs in Gene 1)
gene2_snps.csv (genotype matrix for SNPs in Gene 2)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the genotype data and phenotype vector ;; 2. Run the gene-gene interaction test using the GGI function ;; 3. Print and plot the interaction results
workflows.code:
library(GeneGeneInteR)
data(GGI.data)
result <- GGI(Y = response, snps1 = gene1, snps2 = gene2, method = "CCA")
print(result)
